Cancer cells differ from normal cells in culture in several ways: normal cells typically have limited division capacity (Hayflick limit), while cancer cells can divide indefinitely; cancer cells lack contact inhibition, while normal cells stop dividing when they contact neighboring cells; and cancer cells often proliferate to higher densities than normal cells. However, both cancer cells and normal cells generally require a surface for attachment to grow in culture, as they are anchorage-dependent for proliferation (though some cancer cells may become anchorage-independent, this is not universal).  

Final answer: (C)
